text:
anya: pushed a tweak to the kernel-bench harness this morning, nightly flagged a regression on AVX512 long-seqlen path. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/bench/+/PR-482 :eyes:
perf-bot: nightly-sweep results (1976543200): candidate_kv_v7 on hpc-avx512: median +8%, p99 +22% vs baseline_kv_v5. Regression concentrated at seqlen=1024..4096 and warm-KV path. Full logs: https://ci.redwood/runs/98765/logs
mike: can you paste a minimal repro command? want to run locally on my dev node.
devon: repro that matches CI:```bash
python -m bench.runner \
  --kernel candidate_kv_v7 \
  --model gpt2-medium \
  --seqlen 2048 \
  --batch-size 1 \
  --runs 150 \
  --device avx512 \
  --warm-kv true
```
output snippet (p99): `608.3 ms` vs baseline `498.1 ms` (same machine). logs show extra memcpy+transpose in the AVX512 path.
rachel: my gut is that the new matmul microkernel added a fallback that does a 64-byte misaligned copy for seqs > 1024 due to simd width rounding. int8 quant kernels are hit worse because we add a pretransposition step.
samir: I can add a focused microbench: toggle alignment and warm-kv. Plan: 1) seqlen sweep {128,512,1024,2048,4096} 2) warm-kv on/off 3) batch 1 and batch 8. Will run nightly and post diffs.
anya: thanks — two asks: 1) can we gate candidate_kv_v7 from autotune selection if it fails arch-aware p99 check? 2) add a microbench in perf CI that explicitly tests the KV-warm path at long seqlens (so we don't miss regressions that only show up after kv cache hits). :thumbsup:
mike: propose a quick scoring/gating heuristic we can add to the harness:```python
# scoring: combine median + p99 sensitivity + kv-warm penalty
score = median_latency + 2 * (p99_latency - median_latency) + kv_warm_penalty + arch_penalty
# accept if score <= baseline_score * 1.05
```
devon: suggestion on seqlen buckets for the harness switch logic: [1-64, 65-256, 257-1024, 1025-4096, 4097+]. autotuner should prefer kernels that are dominant across the largest contiguous bucket, not just point-median wins. also add a check for extra-copy count in the trace.
rachel: one more note: quant backend uses a different packing routine that assumes 32-byte alignment; adding a 64-byte forced alignment on the AVX512 path made the buffer allocator insert an extra copy. maybe revert alignment or change allocator to provide 64-byte aligned buffers.
samir: I'll submit a PR with the microbench variants + warm-kv toggles and update the nightly matrix. assigning to myself, will post results by EOD tomorrow.
perf-bot: attached: https://ci.redwood/runs/98765/artifacts/avx512-4096-warm-kv-trace.tar.gz (trace contains memcpy counts and kernel selection records).
anya: great. once samir has the microbench, let's re-run autotune with gating enabled. if the candidate still regresses, we block it from rollout and mark as "needs kernel patch".
mike: also adding a small note to the CI docs to ensure candidate kernels include an "alignment cost" metric (counts of copies) in their report.
devon: i'll add a tiny harness wrapper that parses trace for memcpy ops and emits `alignment_copy_count` in the bench summary.
anya: perfect. thanks team. :rocket:
